claim: Chez Pipo, 13 rue Bavastro in the port district, has built its fame on socca, a wood-fired chickpea galette and undisputed star of its menu.
quote: Star incontestée de tous nos plats ! On lui doit la célébrité de Chez Pipo.

claim: René Socca, just off Rue Pairolière, is the no-frills budget pick for socca that locals favour.
quote: René Socca offers a straightforward and delicious experience, located just off Rue Pairolière, serving consistently good, fresh socca at very reasonable prices.

claim: Niçoise specialties to seek include socca, pissaladière (caramelised onions and anchovies on thin crust, no cheese), pan-bagnat, salade niçoise, petits farcis, daube, tourte de blettes and ratatouille.
quote: A cross between pizza and tart, made with caramelized onions, anchovies, and Niçois olives on a thin crust.

claim: An authentic salade niçoise contains only raw vegetables plus hard-boiled egg — no potatoes, no green beans — per Jacques Médecin's 1972 codification.
quote: A true Niçoise Salad only has raw vegetables, with the only cooked item being hard-boiled eggs. There are no green beans nor potatoes in this authentic recipe.

claim: Cours Saleya hosts a flower-and-produce market Tuesday–Sunday (roughly 6 am–1:30 pm for produce, flowers until late afternoon) and a 200-stall antiques market on Mondays.
quote: The Cours Saleya Flower Market takes place from Tuesday to Saturday from 6.00 am to 5.00 pm and on Sunday from 6.00 am to 1.30 pm.

claim: Flaveur, run by the Tourteaux brothers, is the only two-Michelin-star restaurant in Nice, while Le Chantecler at Le Negresco holds one star alongside JAN, Les Agitateurs, ONICE, L'Aromate, Racines and Pure & V.
quote: As the only restaurant in Nice with two Michelin stars to its name, I know you can expect a stand-out experience

claim: Le Chantecler inside Hôtel Negresco on the Promenade des Anglais is led by MOF 2015 chef Virginie Basselot and pairs historic Belle Époque elegance with a summer terrace.
quote: MOF 2015, Virginie Basselot, is at the helm of its fine dining restaurant, Le Chantecler.

claim: Bistrot d'Antoine at 27 rue de la Préfecture holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand and is the go-to affordable French bistro in Vieux Nice (closed Sun-Mon; reservations essential).
quote: The restaurant has earned the Bib Gourmand designation for good quality, good value cooking.

claim: La Merenda, run by former two-Michelin-star chef Dominique Le Stanc, serves Niçoise classics (pissaladière, tripe niçoise, stockfish, tourte de blettes) with no phone, no credit cards, and in-person reservations only.
quote: It serves just twenty people, has a former head chef of a two Michelin starred restaurant and yet takes no reservations other than in person and does not even have a telephone.

claim: Chez Acchiardo is a 90-year-old family-run trattoria in Vieux Nice serving petits farcis niçois, salade niçoise and traditional grilled meats in a stone-walled dining room.
quote: Chez Acchiardo is a family-run restaurant located in the old town of Nice, serving traditional Italian cuisine for over 90 years.

claim: Olive & Artichaut on rue Sainte Réparate is a Bib Gourmand Mediterranean bistro that consistently scores top marks for value and creativity.
quote: Olive & Artichaut is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide France, recognized for good quality and good value cooking.

claim: Tourte de blettes, a chard tart studded with raisins and pine nuts that can be sweet or savoury, exemplifies the originality of Niçoise cuisine where vegetables are used in desserts.
quote: Chard pie is a perfect illustration of the originality of Niçoise cuisine, where vegetables are also used in sweet recipes.

claim: L'Effervescence in the Old Town is Nice's only champagne bar, pouring more than 80 champagnes alongside gourmet plates Tuesday–Saturday 6 pm–midnight.
quote: L'Effervescence is Nice's only champagne bar... serving gourmet food, sushi, fine wines and over 80 different kinds of champagne.
